purpose: Represent high-control/coercive systems and hate/extremism classifications without turning contested labels into intrinsic properties of people or organizations.
high_control_rule: Do not store cult=true. Store observable dimensions, named analytical models, legal findings and evidence status.

high_control_dimensions.description: Authority concentrated around a leader whose legitimacy is treated as exceptional or overriding.
A binding worldview that can become self-sealing when competing information is delegitimized.
Rules, surveillance, discipline, resource control, labor control or sanctions shaping member behavior.
Repeated social, informational or emotional processes reinforcing group commitments and interpretations.
Limits on outside sources, relationships or critical information.
Formal or informal retaliation for criticism, questioning, disclosure or exit.
Economic, social, housing, labor, identity or relationship dependence that raises exit costs.
Systematic observation, reporting or documentation of member behavior.
Material extraction substantially beyond ordinary voluntary association, especially when coercive or deceptive.
Control over intimate relationships or sexual behavior, especially where coercion or exploitation is documented.
Threats, collateral, social exclusion, financial loss, legal pressure or fear making exit unusually costly.
Internal mechanisms block external oversight, investigation or correction.

analytical_models.author: Janja Lalich
analytical_models.limitation: Not a universal legal definition and not proof that every group displaying one feature is abusive.

anchor_cases.use: Anchor showing why a high-control analysis should connect to observable coercion and adjudicated conduct rather than unusual beliefs alone.

classification_power_model.rule: A classification is a dated relationship between classifier, methodology and target; it is not an eternal property of the target.

classifier_seeds.name: Southern Poverty Law Center
methodological_notes: SPLC says it classifies organizations, not individuals, as hate groups.
Its methodology uses official statements/principles, leader statements and activities, plus multiple information sources.
Its historical map methodology has changed over time and should retain year/version context.

classifier_seeds.name: ADL H.E.A.T. Map
methodological_notes: Tracks specific incidents of hate, extremism, antisemitism and terrorism.
Uses news/media, government documents, victim reports, extremist-related sources and ADL investigations.
Incident mapping should not be silently converted into organization-level guilt or classification.

safeguards: Religious, political or unconventional beliefs alone do not establish coercive control.
A watchdog classification does not establish criminality unless criminal conduct is separately documented.
Different classifiers may disagree; store disagreement rather than flattening it.
A person should not inherit a group-level label merely through association, attendance, readership or social contact.
Classification records require dates because organizations, leadership and methodology can change.
